method: Ranked by claude-sonnet-5-5, which read 13 of 14 shortlisted pieces

picks.title: End‑to‑End 4‑Bit Training
picks.author: Thinking Machines Lab
picks.why_it_matters: Explains how NVFP4 block scaling works and why 4-bit forward passes with MXFP8 backward passes (re-quantization, stochastic rounding) cut quantization bias and give real wall-clock speedups.

picks.title: The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development
picks.author: Dwarkesh Patel
picks.why_it_matters: Argues AI research is verifiable enough to automate like math, using the transformer as a case study; a long, opinionated take to test against.

picks.title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
picks.author: bookofjoe
picks.why_it_matters: Claude helped decode Gödel's shorthand notebooks and reconstruct a near-proof of the axiom of choice's independence, checked in Coq; shows what AI can and can't verify.

picks.title: Nasser’s long road to Suez
picks.author: Jack Dickens
picks.why_it_matters: Treats Suez as an Egyptian decision rooted in 1882 to 1942 humiliations, not just great-power maneuvering; the 'Lesseps' radio code detail is a good hook.

picks.title: Fugitive imagination
picks.author: Shahram Khosravi
picks.why_it_matters: An anthropologist and former border-crosser argues that smugglers and fugitives practice a form of imagination states treat as a threat; the smuggler-as-architect idea is the core.
